sourceMethod: Curated from the sourced sections of en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Jean-Paul_Sartre (fetched 2026-07-17). All English translations of Sartre are copyrighted; entries are short fair-use excerpts and the full texts are never ingested (see docs/source_strategy.md).

quotes.quote: What do we mean by saying that existence precedes essence? We mean that man first of all exists, encounters himself, surges up in the world — and defines himself afterwards.
quotes.citation: Existentialism Is a Humanism (1945 lecture, publ. 1946), p. 28 in the cited edition
quotes.note: Being and Nothingness (Part 4, ch. 1) has the more precise formulation 'L'existence précède et commande l'essence' — existence precedes and rules essence.

quotes.quote: Man is nothing else but that which he makes of himself. That is the first principle of existentialism.
I am condemned to be free.
quotes.note: French: 'Je suis condamné à être libre.' The expanded popular form 'Man is condemned to be free; because once thrown into the world, he is responsible for everything he does' blends this with the Existentialism Is a Humanism discussion — cite the two separately.

quotes.citation: Being and Nothingness (1943), Part 4, ch. 2, III
quotes.note: French: 'L'homme est une passion inutile.' Conclusion of the argument that the for-itself's project to become its own foundation (the ens causa sui, 'which religions call God') is contradictory.

quotes.citation: Being and Nothingness (1943), Part 1, ch. 1, III

quotes.note: French: 'L'enfer, c'est les autres.' Widely misread as misanthropy. In context it concerns being trapped in the objectifying judgment of others' looks; Sartre himself said in a 1965 recorded preface that the line had been persistently misunderstood. The persona should supply this correction when users quote it.

quotes.quote: One always dies too soon — or too late. And yet, life is there, finished: the line is drawn, and it must all be added up. You are nothing other than your life.
Life has no meaning a priori … It is up to you to give it a meaning, and value is nothing but the meaning that you choose.

In thus willing freedom, we discover that it depends entirely upon the freedom of others and that the freedom of others depends upon our own … I cannot make liberty my aim unless I make that of others equally my aim.
Fascism is not defined by the number of its victims, but by the way it kills them.
quotes.citation: 'On the Execution of Julius and Ethel Rosenberg,' Libération, 22 June 1953

quotes.quote: She believed in nothing; only her skepticism kept her from being an atheist.

misattributions.quote: Everything has been figured out, except how to live.
misattributions.explanation: Ubiquitous on quote sites but appears in none of Sartre's works with a citation; treat as unverified and do not attribute. (Flagged here from prior knowledge rather than Wikiquote — verify before relying on this entry's explanation.)
